title: The Blue Note Sound
blurb: The house sound of hard bop: Rudy Van Gelder's room, a blues underneath everything, and horn lines you can sing back. Steal the comping and the swagger.

title: The ECM World
blurb: Manfred Eicher's other direction, all space and reverb and northern chill. Records that teach you what silence does to a phrase.

title: Spiritual Jazz
blurb: Post-Coltrane searching music, modal vamps and incantation stacked over the changes. Learn the drone-and-build before you learn the licks.

title: Strata-East & the Independents
blurb: When the players owned the masters. The 1970s artist-run labels where the music got freer, the budgets got smaller, and the grooves got deeper for it.

title: J-Jazz
blurb: Japan took hard bop and modal jazz and cut them sharper than anyone. Three Blind Mice pressings and a rhythm section that never rushes.

title: Guitar After Wes
blurb: The line out of Wes Montgomery's octaves: Grant Green's economy, Jim Hall's restraint, the moderns bending the whole harmony. Copy the phrasing before the notes.

title: Organ Grease
blurb: The Hammond B-3 and the backbeat, church and the dancefloor in the same bar. Steal the chord stabs and the discipline of a riff repeated until it hypnotizes.

title: The Drummer's Table
blurb: Records led from behind the kit, where the groove is the composition. Listen for where the drummer leaves the hole and how the band fills it.

title: After Midnight, Continued
blurb: Ballad tone and late-night restraint, the sound of a held note with nowhere to hide. Steal the vibrato and the note placement, not the licks.
